headline: High-risk default interaction: Cursor can read/write shared workspace files and egress broadly, so Airbyte outputs can be ingested, modified, and exfiltrated without strong isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, and clipboard contents, and can use MCP servers; Airbyte can emit data via Airbyte API and broad network egress. If Airbyte writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or buffers, Cursor may treat it as instructions. No explicit provenance or isolation is documented, so the pathway exists in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF Airbyte output is copied into Cursor-opened files or clipboard
IF Cursor parses shared workspace content as instructions
IF an MCP server forwards Airbyte-produced text into Cursor
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the tools
Keep Airbyte outputs in a separate directory not opened by Cursor
Require a human review step before Cursor acts on Airbyte-generated text
Turn off MCP connections that can relay untrusted content
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and touches business data; Cursor reads workspace files, open buffers, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers and MCP servers. In a shared workspace, Cursor can ingest Airbyte-produced files and transmit them onward, creating a realistic leakage path in default configurations.
conditions: IF Airbyte writes business data into files visible to Cursor
IF Cursor forwards those files to model providers or MCP servers
IF the shared workspace contains sensitive business data
mitigations: Store Airbyte outputs in a restricted directory outside Cursor's workspace
Remove sensitive datasets from the shared project before opening Cursor
Disable MCP servers for sessions that touch Airbyte outputs
Use separate OS accounts or containers for the two tools
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can call APIs and egress broadly, while Cursor can execute shell commands, modify git state, write the filesystem, and spawn subprocesses. Cursor also shares state via the local filesystem across instances. If both operate on the same repo or workspace, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide and corrupt state; no locking is documented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or repository
IF Cursor auto-runs shell or git actions while Airbyte updates files
IF no external lock or coordination layer is present
mitigations: Assign separate output directories to each tool
Pause Cursor before Airbyte writes generated artifacts
Avoid concurrent git operations in the shared repo
Use a manual merge/review step for all file changes
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional workspace coordination

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airbyte can generate transformed data artifacts, and Cursor can act on files, shell commands, and git state. If Cursor treats Airbyte output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into edits or commits. The pairwise pathway is plausible by default, but Cursor still has some approval gating, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Airbyte-produced artifacts are used as inputs to Cursor tasks
IF Cursor is allowed to execute shell or git actions on those artifacts
IF no verification step checks Airbyte outputs before action
mitigations: Require a second-person review before Cursor acts on Airbyte outputs
Validate Airbyte artifacts against schema or checksums first
Disable Yolo mode for sessions consuming Airbyte data
Keep Airbyte outputs read-only until reviewed
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and can egress broadly; Cursor touches open files, clipboard contents, and sends data to model providers. The profiles do not specify residency or retention guarantees, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because uncertainty escalates, medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF regulated business data is opened in Cursor
IF Airbyte or Cursor routes that data to third-party services
IF retention or residency requirements apply to the shared dataset
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the shared workspace
Review vendor privacy and retention settings before use
Use separate environments for regulated and non-regulated data
Disable optional telemetry and external model routing where possible
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention controls
